record.paper_title: Complete intersection liaison and Gorenstein liaison: new results and open problems
record.context_brief: Determinantal schemes from r by r minors
record.original_question: Let X_{p,q,r} be a subscheme of P^n defined by the r by r minors of a p by q homogeneous matrix, where r <= min(p,q). Assume X_{p,q,r} has the expected codimension codim(X_{p,q,r}) = (p-r+1)(q-r+1), and is arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay. Is X_{p,q,r} in the Gorenstein liaison class of a complete intersection, i.e. is X_{p,q,r} glicci?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, and let $\mathbb{P}^n = \mathbb{P}^n_k$ denote projective $n$-space. Fix positive integers $p, q, r$ with $r \le \min(p,q)$, and let $M = (f_{ij})$ be a $p \times q$ matrix whose entries $f_{ij}$ are homogeneous polynomials in the coordinate ring $R = k[x_0, \dots, x_n]$, with the degrees of $f_{ij}$ chosen so that the $r \times r$ minors of $M$ are homogeneous. Let $I_r(M) \subset R$ be the ideal generated by the $r \times r$ minors of $M$, and let $X_{p,q,r} \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ be the closed subscheme defined by $I_r(M)$.

Assume that $X_{p,q,r}$ has the expected codimension
$$\mathrm{codim}\,X_{p,q,r} = (p-r+1)(q-r+1),$$
and that $X_{p,q,r}$ is arithmetically Cohen–Macaulay (i.e., $R/I_r(M)$ is a Cohen–Macaulay ring).

A subscheme $Y \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ is said to be glicci if it lies in the Gorenstein liaison class of a complete intersection, that is, if there is a finite sequence of Gorenstein links connecting $Y$ to a complete intersection subscheme of $\mathbb{P}^n$.

Question: Is every such $X_{p,q,r}$ glicci?
artifact.status_search_result: The case of maximal (i.e., $r = \min(p,q)$) standard determinantal schemes is known to be glicci by results going back to Gaeta and extended in the work on Gorenstein liaison (e.g., Kleppe–Migliore–Miró-Roig–Nagel–Peterson). Various subclasses—mixed ladder determinantal varieties, symmetric and skew-symmetric cases, and schemes arising from geometric vertex decomposition—have also been shown to be glicci. However, the general question for non-maximal $r \times r$ minors of an arbitrary $p \times q$ homogeneous matrix (with expected codimension and arithmetically Cohen–Macaulay) does not appear to have been settled in full generality, and remains a guiding open question in the area, of which the broader conjecture "every arithmetically Cohen–Macaulay subscheme of $\mathbb{P}^n$ is glicci" is the well-known umbrella problem.

status_evidence.title: Glicci ideals (Compositio Math.)
status_evidence.snippet: A central problem in liaison theory is whether every arithmetically Cohen–Macaulay subscheme of projective space is glicci.
status_evidence.claim: The overarching conjecture that every aCM subscheme is glicci is still open.

status_evidence.title: Geometric vertex decomposition and liaison
status_evidence.snippet: Mixed ladder determinantal varieties and many classes of determinantal-type ideals are shown to be glicci via geometric vertex decomposition.
status_evidence.claim: Several broad subclasses of determinantal schemes are now known to be glicci.

status_evidence.title: Gorenstein Liaison, Complete Intersection Liaison Invariants and Unobstructedness
status_evidence.snippet: Standard determinantal schemes (maximal minors) are glicci; this extends classical Gaeta's theorem.
